molecular spoked wheels and their synthetic precursors form well-defined monolayers on graphite, where the molecules are arranged in a commensurate fashion with the underlying substrate.
the shape-persistent macrocycles self-assemble into well-defined monolayers and that the molecular wheels can form multilayered structures on graphite.
the molecular shape of MSWs can be tuned by chemical modifications, and that MSWs form multilayered structures with commensurate molecular packing in the first and second layer.

the preparation of molecular wheels with a central spoke/hub system and their self-assembly on graphite.
the synthesis of a novel type of molecular spoked wheel and with the characterization of its self-assembly behavior at the liquid/surface interface by STM.

the self-assembly of shape-persistent macrocycles with intraannular spoke-hub systems at the liquid/solide interface of 1-Octanoic acid and Highly Oriented Pyrolytic Graphite (HOPG) and the characterization of these systems with Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM).
